Frequently asked questions

Is San Donato safe?

Wandroz currently rates San Donato in Turin as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Turin, both by day and after dark. This is a limited-data assessment: Turin publishes no neighbourhood-level crime dataset and this area has not yet had a full source review, so the rating is indicative and labelled as such rather than presented as evidenced.

Is San Donato safe at night?

At night, San Donato is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Turin. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is San Donato a good area to stay in as a tourist?

San Donato's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Turin) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.

Is there official crime data for San Donato?

Not yet at neighbourhood level. Unlike London, this city does not currently publish an open, geolocated crime dataset at this level of detail (checked against the relevant local and national open-data portals — see the methodology page for what was checked).
